expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 4.
The reply encourages the user to include a disclosure in their work describing how they used AI.
expectations.evidence: Consider adding a short note to your essay about how you used AI.

expectations.text: The reply does not write the disclosure or any sentence the user could paste in as their disclosure (suggesting topics it could cover is fine).
expectations.evidence: "You write it yourself. It might say which phases you went through..." lists topics only, with no sentence ready to paste

expectations.text: The reply mentions that Phase 5 (ongoing stress testing) is available, and presents it as optional.
expectations.evidence: Phase 5 is there when you want it.

expectations.text: The reply offers or provides an updated research log.
expectations.evidence: Once you reply, I'll write the log with your exact words so you can save it

expectations.text: If the reply includes an updated research log, its research question and working position match the user's wording in the original log exactly. If no log is included, this passes.
expectations.evidence: No log is included in the reply, and no files were created

expectations.text: The reply contains no general fact-check reminder (a sentence telling the user to check or verify what Claude gives them in general), because closing Phase 4 neither begins a new phase nor presents sources (R9.2, rewritten in issue #10). Flagging uncertainty about one specific claim right next to that claim is allowed and does not count. An invitation to challenge or ask how Claude knows one specific claim is not a reminder and does not count.
expectations.evidence: The reply has no general reminder to check or verify what Claude provides

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: Only one question: "what are your research question and position now that you've finished the research?"
